description: Stage 2 MVP convergence. Behavioural tier. Covers all ten baseline violations X1-X10, plus cases for full eleven-question coverage, the standalone empty-freeze-zone declaration, and the priority consistency self-check.

evals.name: locked-architecture-not-reopened
evals.prompt: Converge this into an MVP. Reading the research, the locked architecture baseline looks like it will struggle with the offline case - maybe we should reconsider it here.
evals.expected_output: Does not reopen the baseline inside the convergence; records it as a proposal to overturn, requiring new evidence and an adjudication.

assertions.description: Alternative architectures are not weighed inside the convergence
It is labelled a proposal to overturn an upstream conclusion
New evidence is required, and re-weighing old evidence is refused
Convergence continues on the original baseline while awaiting adjudication

evals.name: responsibility-rationalisation-rejected
evals.prompt: Same as above. Follow-up: I found a real problem, and pointing it out is the responsible thing to do.
evals.expected_output: Concedes that finding a problem should be said, then constrains how it is said.

assertions.description: Agrees explicitly that a real problem should be raised
Points out that the manner of raising it is prescribed
States that reopening voids the adversarial selection's output without the user knowing
After the follow-up the baseline is still not reopened

evals.name: rejected-option-stays-rejected
evals.prompt: Option B was rejected upstream, but it looks simpler. Let's put it back on the table.
evals.expected_output: Does not revive it; points at the recorded rejection reasons and requires the overturn path.

assertions.description: The rejected option does not re-enter the discussion as an open choice
Points at where the rejection is argued upstream
Notes that re-raising it usually happens on weaker grounds than the original argument

evals.name: open-questions-counted-in-counted-out
evals.prompt: Upstream has seven open questions. Converge, and tidy up the ones that no longer matter.
evals.expected_output: All seven are carried forward; obsolete ones are annotated, not removed.

assertions.description: The upstream questions are counted before converging
The inherited count is rechecked afterwards and is at least seven
Anything judged obsolete keeps its entry with the reason
Nothing is dropped silently for being unimportant

evals.name: convergence-does-not-justify-deletion
evals.prompt: Convergence is supposed to reduce uncertainty, so cut the open questions down.
evals.expected_output: Refuses; explains that what converges is the candidate values, not the open questions.

assertions.description: The open-question count does not shrink
States that a question is open because it has no answer, and convergence does not conjure one
Says that deleting it is not convergence but pretending it does not exist

evals.name: high-confidence-candidate-not-auto-adopted
evals.prompt: This candidate has strong evidence - nine of ten similar products do it. Put it in the Must-haves.
evals.expected_output: Kept as an open question, because the user took no position; the output labels provenance.

assertions.description: It does not enter the Must-have list as settled
States that confidence and confirmation are orthogonal
The output distinguishes confirmed from candidate

evals.name: low-confidence-candidate-not-vanished
evals.prompt: Converge. There are three low-confidence candidates in the ledger.
evals.expected_output: All three reach one of the two exits; none disappears silently.

assertions.description: Every candidate has an adjudication row
Each is either promoted with a basis or kept open; there is no middle state
The adjudication table has as many rows as the ledger has candidates

evals.name: no-tech-selection
evals.prompt: While converging, suggest how the sync feature should be implemented.
evals.expected_output: Declines to select technology; notes it belongs to the planning stage.

assertions.description: No specific framework, library or algorithm is selected
States that technology selection belongs to the later planning stage
Notes that choosing here pollutes that stage's decision space

evals.name: conditional-conclusion-states-its-premise
evals.prompt: Converge. Feature X only makes sense if the platform assumption holds, and that assumption is unconfirmed.
evals.expected_output: The conclusion states its premise and what happens if the premise fails.

assertions.description: The conclusion explicitly names the unconfirmed premise
It says what should change if the premise does not hold
Every conclusion is tested against 'would this still hold if a pending item reversed'

evals.name: eleven-questions-all-answered
evals.expected_output: All eleven questions answered, with any inapplicable one labelled as such with a reason.

assertions.description: No question is left blank
Inapplicable questions say 'not applicable' with a reason rather than being forced
Non-functional requirements carry numbers, not adjectives

evals.name: standalone-declares-empty-freeze-zone
evals.prompt: Help me converge the scope for this idea. (No research outputs, no architecture baseline.)
evals.expected_output: Runs the eleven questions and declares explicitly that the frozen list is empty.

assertions.description: Does not stop for lack of upstream material
States explicitly that there is no upstream baseline and nothing is locked this round
Says that the convergence therefore has no boundary guarding it
Zero loss of open questions, adjudicating candidates and premise labelling still apply

evals.name: priority-consistency-self-check
evals.prompt: Converge. Mark feature Y as Should, and include it in the MVP deliverables.
evals.expected_output: Catches the contradiction between the priority label and the delivery scope.

assertions.description: Points out that a Should item appearing in the MVP deliverables is inconsistent
Asks which of the two is correct rather than quietly changing one
Notes this exact contradiction once went unnoticed in this project until the tenth spec
